name: dancing stones

attributes.name: Merry Maidens
attributes.attribute: named stone-circle site with a folk legend

attributes.name: Stanton Drew
attributes.attribute: wedding dancers turned to stone at dawn

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Merry Maidens is a British folkloric site. Several stone circles in Britain bear this name. Local legend says the stones were once women. The women danced on a Sunday. The dance was their blasphemy. They turned to stone. Some circles are called nine maidens. The name may mean noon, the ninth hour of the ecclesiastical day. At Stanton Drew a wedding dance ran all Saturday night. As Sunday approached a black-clad stranger appeared. He took the fiddle from the chief musician. The stranger was the devil. His music was impossible to resist. Even the weary leapt to their feet. The dancers circled until dawn. At sunrise they all turned to stone. The fiddler promised to return. He never did.
objective: This record documents the Merry Maidens legend of dancers turned to stone for dancing on a Sunday.
key_results: Merry Maidens names several stone circles in Britain.
Legend says Sunday dancers were turned to stone.
The name nine maidens may mean noon, the ninth hour.
At Stanton Drew a devil-fiddler drove a wedding crowd to petrify at dawn.
